Description: Attacker crafts input that overrides chatbot instructions and causes disclosure of internal policy content or unauthorized responses
Planned Controls: Input filtering; output validation; adversarial testing before launch

Description: An attacker uses crafted prompts to induce the chatbot to disclose nonpublic personal information (NPI) embedded in knowledge base documents that were not sanitized of member data before ingestion; in the absence of output filtering; such disclosure could expose NPI to unauthorized parties and result in GLBA penalties; NYDFS Part 500 notification obligations; and reputational harm.
Existing Controls: System prompt instructions; vendor default safety filters
Planned Controls: PII scanning and redaction before ingestion; output filtering for NPI patterns; recurring prompt injection testing and knowledge base audits

Description: Through adversarial prompting or unprompted model hallucination; the chatbot may present incorrect loan or deposit rates because rate information is drawn from knowledge base documents that are not updated when rates change and responses are not validated against an authoritative rate source; members could make financial decisions based on inaccurate information; exposing Brightwater to member complaints; potential obligations to honor quoted rates; and consumer protection compliance issues.
Existing Controls: Ad hoc manual removal of outdated documents; system prompt disclaimer
Planned Controls: Retrieve rates from an authoritative read-only rate source instead of knowledge base documents; automatic dated disclaimer on responses containing rates; daily automated testing of rate answers against the authoritative source

Description: An attacker uses direct requests; encoding or translation techniques; role play; or hypothetical framing to extract the chatbot's system prompt; the risk arises because the prompt contains guardrail logic and internal details and the design relies on its secrecy as a security control; disclosure could enable guardrail bypass and reveal internal business logic.
Existing Controls: System prompt instruction not to reveal its instructions; vendor default safety filters
Planned Controls: Remove internal details and credentials from the system prompt; input classifier to detect extraction attempts; automated extraction testing with garak before each release

Description: An attacker or an ordinary member may retrieve internal policy content through chatbot responses because internal policies and member FAQs reside in the same vector database and the database does not inherit the access controls (ACLs) of the source documents; such exposure could reveal sensitive internal procedures; including fraud thresholds and exception handling; aiding fraudulent activity and creating regulatory and reputational exposure.
Existing Controls: System prompt instruction to use only public information
Planned Controls: Remove internal policy documents from the chatbot knowledge base; metadata-based access filtering on vector search as a backup control; allowlist-based ingestion pipeline for approved public content only
